newsitem.title: USA: Couple accused in baby killing return to New Jersey.
newsitem.headline: Couple accused in baby killing return to New Jersey.

text.p: A teenage couple accused of killing their newborn child have been allowed to return to their homes in New Jersey to await trial, state prison officials said Friday.

Amy Grossberg and Brian Peterson left Delaware Friday afternoon in separate private cars for their homes in Wyckoff, N.J., wearing electronic monitoring devices, Delaware Correction Department spokesman Anthony Farina said.

Grossberg and Peterson, both 18, were released on $300,000 bail last week pending trial but were required to remain in Delaware until arrangements could be made for out-of-state electronic monitoring.

The bail conditions for Grossberg and Peterson included provisions that they live at home with their families in Wyckoff, be electronically monitored and observe a curfew of 6 a.m. to 8 p.m., which would allow them to work and take classes.
Peterson also had to surrender his passport.

Under arrangements worked out between officials in Delaware and Bergen County, New Jersey, any minor curfew violations would be investigated by county officials. The Delaware attorney general's office would be responsible for dealing with more serious bail violations, Farina said.
Grossberg and Peterson had been staying in separate homes in Delaware and were electronically monitored since last week's bail order.
The two were high school sweethearts in New Jersey before going on to college last fall in separate states.

According to court records, Peterson helped Grossberg deliver a baby boy Nov. 12 in a motel room in Newark, Delaware, and disposed of the body in a dumpster behind the motel. The motel was not far from the University of Delaware where Grossberg was a student.

They were indicted last month on one charge of intentional murder in the first-degree and a second charge of murder in the first-degree by abuse and neglect. They face a possible death penalty if convicted on the intentional murder charge in a trial set to begin Sept. 9.
The state medical examiner has said in a preliminary report the infant was alive when born and then fatally injured by being shaken and receiving a blow to the head.

At a court hearing last month, defence attorneys indicated their experts believed the infant would not have survived its own congenital deformities or the medical problems suffered by Grossberg early in her pregnancy.
